decision.conclusion: Both final policies complete the nominal native chain with zero sampled torso support during walking and quiet return to the fixed default controller. Training with measured encoder positions reduces equal-stage moving torso support and forward mean error in all four selected adverse cases, but worsens absolute mean turn error in all five cases and mean foot-contact slip in three. Residual support remains substantial in some individual stages. All eight adverse chains fail both the original 2 s and extended 8 s default quiet screens. These results support the sensing correction as a faithful training interface, not an unqualified policy or foundation-completion claim.

class_requirement.requirement: Low stance, torso above the ground rather than belly-supported, reference-like stepping, and motion in the commanded direction. The course explicitly accepts slower-than-commanded travel; top speeds should match achievable response.
class_requirement.interpretation: Sustained torso support in selected cases remains a failure to establish the no-belly property. Descriptive force thresholds do not replace that requirement.

decision.selection_scope: No automatic installation or replacement of current default, entry/exit, or walking policies. Combine this bounded native evidence with the separately owned completed randomized GPU comparison before choosing the next experiment.

training.comparison: Only the walking actor training observation mode changes: legacy_true versus deployment_measured. Both final policies are evaluated with measured joint positions in this native study. Final manifests, model files and strict export receipts are copied and hashed in the artifact bundle.

native_protocol.sequence: entry; walk activation; forward +0.10 m/s for 2 s; zero for 1 s; backward -0.10 m/s for 2 s; turn +0.20 rad/s for 2 s; zero for 2 s; exit; standing hold; default activation; default forward +0.10 m/s for 2 s; default zero for 8 s
native_protocol.bias_and_actuation: All actors observe q_true + encoder_bias. Initialization and slew state seed from measured position. Controller and driver clamps and the walking slew operate in measured coordinates; physical target equals driver target minus bias, before fixed latency. Captured PD scales multiply all command updates. Mechanical joint limits are unchanged.
native_protocol.case_selection: Nominal plus two previously selected exact GPU startup worlds (seed101/world11 and seed303/world3), each under sphere-only and foot-end-union material assumptions, paired across the two final actors.
native_protocol.material_scope: Sphere-only applies captured foot sphere friction while retaining original lower-leg hull material. Foot-end union applies the same captured material and priority to foot spheres and lower-leg hulls. Union is a separate modeling assumption; neither native full-hull case is a GPU trajectory replay.
native_protocol.pairing: Compiled model bytes and all 489 recorded entry physical/command samples are identical within each pair. The state is continuous through later controller transitions.

metric_definitions.moving_support: Equal mean of the forward, backward and turn stage means of recorded torso normal force divided by model mass times 9.81. Full per-stage quantiles, support fractions and observed spans remain in raw review.
metric_definitions.forward_error: Absolute difference between stage-mean body-frame forward velocity and requested +0.10 m/s; includes stage transients. This is not per-sample RMSE.
metric_definitions.turn_error: Absolute difference between stage-mean unwrapped-world-heading rate and requested +0.20 rad/s; includes stage transients. World-heading rate is not body angular velocity. Effective heading assistance is separately recorded in the independent review.
metric_definitions.foot_slip: Within each moving stage, sum(normal force times contact-point tangential relative speed) / sum(normal force), then equal mean across the three moving stages. Uses the actual foot sphere/lower-leg hull contacts. This differs from GPU contact-gated foot-site horizontal velocity.
metric_definitions.quiet: All selected final 0.5 s samples must have body planar speed <0.02 m/s, absolute world-heading difference rate <0.05 rad/s and every joint speed <0.05 rad/s. At 52 Hz the selected 26 states span 25/52 s. Original 2 s and extended 8 s windows are reported separately. Independent world-XY interval speeds give the same verdict.
metric_definitions.load_thresholds: 0.1%, 1% and 10% bodyweight are descriptive diagnostics, not pass thresholds. Longest support span measures first-to-last recorded samples, not full-bin duration.
metric_definitions.time_alignment: Contact forces, points and relative velocities use the same pre-integration copied state. Stored physical pose is after one 1/520 s step. No claim about unrecorded between-sample contact.

aggregate.quiet_cases: Both nominal arms only; none of the eight adverse chains.

fixed_default_attribution.finding: Earlier fresh default-only controls already fail in these recorded adverse parameter contexts without any Spider history. Bias/gain removal alone did not restore quiet. In the tested bias-zero, gain-one context, restoring the combined nominal body mass, central inertia and inertia frame group restored quiet in all four cases, whereas restoring only COM did not. This is conditional group evidence, not an individual mass/inertia cause or calibrated hardware measurement. The default policy remains unchanged.

independent_review.scope: Independently checks input/export/source hashes, compiled model and paired entry identity, contact decomposition and support/slip, body/world motion and quiet, clamp/gain/bias transforms, and 128 recorded native C++ actor events per controller. The audited raw review bytes remain unchanged.

visual_review.status: Inspected both metric plots and six saved-state snapshots from each of three side-by-side comparisons. Full comparison videos are included; rendering uses saved states without integrating new physics.
visual_review.observations: The nominal arms show a low walking stance and similar standing poses after exit. The adverse cases show low clearance and different leg/body orientation through the default zero tail, consistent with recorded support and drift. The camera follows the robot, so displacement and force judgments use saved numeric traces rather than camera motion or visual floor clearance alone.

limitations: One training seed and two startup worlds selected posthoc, each under two material assumptions; this is a bounded paired diagnostic, not a reliability estimate.

Both arms use measured q+b in native deployment; nominal bias zero makes sensing conventions numerically equal. Export encoder metadata describes training and is not used to force legacy sensing during this native comparison.

Only walking network weights and training-contract metadata differ within each pair. The fixed entry/exit and default policies, compiled model and pre-walking history are identical; the later realized state can differ because the walking networks differ.
Both native and training settings differ: native full hull geometry at 520 Hz, training torso hull at 250 Hz; no stochastic sensor noise/IMU delay/reset transfer in native runs.

Tracking RMSE includes stage transients and uses requested constant body XY / world yaw commands. Effective yaw heading assistance is reported separately; worldheading rate is not body-frame angular velocity. No posthoc tracking pass threshold imposed.

Torso load and force-weighted tangential contact speed are verified from recorded 52 Hz contact forces/velocities; relative velocity projection verified for every contact. Contact positions, forces and velocities share prestep copied/forward-solved state. Stored root/joint states are after one 520 Hz step. No unrecorded continuous contact claims.

No physics stepping was performed; absolute contact Jacobians/forces cannot be fully independently reconstructed from 52 Hz poststep records. Their collection algorithm was inspected in the pinned source.

Quiet uses every selected last 0.5 s sample below .02 m/s body planar speed, .05 rad/s unwrapped-worldheading difference and each joint below .05 rad/s; 26 states span 25/52 s. Independent worldXY interval speeds produce the same verdict. 2 s and 8 s windows remain separate.
The fixed default controller has a separately established adverse mass/inertia robustness failure; its failure is not evidence that this walking-actor change alone caused or fixed it.

All target clamps, sampled 3 Nm torque cap and 15 rad/s walking-target slew checks pass; physical soft joint-range excursions are separately quantified. Neither implies measured hardware limits or safety.
No robot, deployment, candidate installation, or training was performed by this audit.
